sourceBrandAssetDeadEnd.why: The dead end is real and confirmed: `source-brand-asset` is release-blocking (src/release/types.ts SEVERITY_POLICY) and its only resolutions (src/release/collect.ts, the source-brand-inline-svg requirement) are an acknowledgement — which releaseBlockers() correctly still treats as blocking (src/release/requirements.ts releaseBlockers: accepted-limitation blocks) — and a future template-layer task. Nothing tonight can honestly clear it: an operator-supplied logo asset has NO consumer that bakes it into inline-SVG markup, so marking such a requirement `resolved` would assert a fix that did not happen. Downgrading its severity would weaken the gate, which the brief forbids. What was done instead, additively and honestly: the existing source-brand-inline-svg requirement now cites WHICH surfaces inside those marks carry the brand (brand-surface:svg-aria-label / svg-symbol-id / svg-text with measured counts and an example value) so the operator is not left guessing what the blocker is. See followUps[0] for the exact unblocking work.

limitations: Runtime-IR-derived surfaces (source-url, image-alt, aria-label) read the PRE-injection template default. A hit may already have been replaced by the content overlay, so those surfaces are reported as high-value hints and are never gated. Only the content run's brand-leak.json carries post-overlay truth, and only that path can escalate to release-blocking.

`dynamic-template-content` is NOT detected. No artifact records the source brand inside dynamically-mounted region content separately from its host route; the evidence only comes into existence with region/route enablement. Declared as detection:'unavailable' rather than reported as zero.

`source-url` counts differ from the audit's baked-html figures (this scan measured 101 on linear vs the audit's 782 URL occurrences in index.html). This scan walks the template runtime IR's href/src/poster/action/srcset props; the baked figure includes the hydration payload, CSS urls and inline style, which this scan does not read. Both numbers are honest measurements of different artifacts.
Findings are capped at 25 per surface (counts stay exact). On linear 169 findings fell past the cap; collect.ts emits an operator warning saying so rather than silently truncating.

src/production/bake.ts was deliberately NOT modified. Its residualSourceUrlOccurrencesInSite still counts only `https://<host>` for network-derived hosts (audit finding BRAND-COUNT). The fuller census lives at QA time instead, because widening bake's result requires src/production/types.ts, outside this agent's ownership set — see changeRequests.

`sourceHostMentionsInHtml` still has no consumer in src/. It was left in place (and is asserted still present) because removing it is a breaking change to a persisted report shape; the new brandSurfaceCensus is the number that means something.

The vacuous `external-requests-only-known-residual` assertion (src/production/qa.ts, filtering observed hosts against knownResidualSourceHosts which for linear IS the source host) was NOT changed. Tightening it would alter the honest network-request blocker path, which the brief explicitly protects.
No SVG path editor. Opaque <path> geometry remains a documented, unaddressed limitation.
